headlines.summary: Clayton’s warning comes ahead of Thanksgiving travel, after separate outages disrupted air travel, Microsoft 365 and some bank transactions.
headlines.article_text: DNI chief Jay Clayton warns of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said modernization and cybersecurity investment may bring temporary interruptions as systems are upgraded. Recent FAA, Microsoft and JPMorgan disruptions had different root causes, and officials say they do not appear to be part of a coordinated cyberattack. Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton testifies during a House Committee on Homeland Security hearing in the Canon House Office Building on Capitol Hill on November 18, 2026 in Washington, DC. Chip Somodevilla | Getty Images Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook. Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions , are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack. Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age. "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said. Read more CNBC politics and policy coverage Jensen Huang slated to appear before House panels Dec. 1; Nvidia lawyer due to testify Dec. 2 Republicans outspent Democrats in record 2026 midterm ad blitz Lisa Cook lawyer signals Fed governor won't attend Trump committee's hearing "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he said. Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours. The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack. Separately, Microsoft said the Outlook outage was caused by "an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade." Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation." Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent said: "No, they shouldn't." "The patches may cause a glitch," he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."
